title: A complete authorisation-code + PKCE round-trip against a local Keycloak realm issues a project session
asA: operator signing in through the project's Keycloak-backed sign-in surface
iWant: the browser to complete a Keycloak authorisation-code round-trip and end up holding a project session cookie
soThat: the project treats me as authenticated on subsequent requests without re-presenting credentials to the realm

acceptanceCriteria.description: The sign-in route redirects to the realm's `authorization_endpoint` with `response_type=code`, PKCE S256 challenge, and a stable `state` value the flow controller stores server-side.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project wired against a local Keycloak realm through the realm-config module and a browser hitting GET `/auth/sign-in`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request is dispatched and the response is inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is a 302 whose `Location` starts with the realm's discovered `authorization_endpoint`; the query carries `response_type=code`, `code_challenge` matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43,128}$`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, a `state` value distinct from any prior observed value in the test collector; no `response_type=token` or `access_type=implicit` is present

acceptanceCriteria.description: The callback exchanges the code at the realm's `token_endpoint` and receives an access token plus id_token.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the realm has minted an authorisation code for the pending flow keyed by the state value from AC-11101-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: the browser follows the realm's redirect back to the project's callback route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the flow controller issues a POST to the realm's `token_endpoint` whose body carries `grant_type=authorization_code`, the returned `code`, `client_id`, `code_verifier` (matching the stored verifier), and `redirect_uri`; the response is a 2xx carrying `access_token` and `id_token`

acceptanceCriteria.description: The callback completes with a Secure HttpOnly session cookie whose value is a project-issued opaque handle, not a Keycloak-minted token.
acceptanceCriteria.given: AC-11101-2 has completed against a realm whose record declares `sessionMode: 'opaque-handle'`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the browser inspects the response cookie jar
acceptanceCriteria.then: a session cookie declared by the project's session-cookie name is set with `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`; the cookie value does not equal the access_token, the id_token, or any refresh_token returned by the realm; the reduced Principal on the next protected-route request carries `principalId` derived from `{realmSlug, sub}` and `provider` equal to the realmSlug
